unit: per job: the valve cover (cylinder head cover) gasket set. One cover on inline engines. On V engines the range runs from one bank to both banks, as noted per class. Not included: a new valve cover, intake manifold gaskets where the manifold has to come off, spark plugs or ignition coils. On some engines with plastic covers (several BMW and Volkswagen engines) the cover is commonly replaced as a whole or the gasket is only sold with it; that costs far more and is noted in the luxury class

finding: The live range of $150-$950 looks about right at both ends, but this check is thinner than we want and the confidence is low. Built totals (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks): economy 2015 Corolla about $155-$522 (1-3 hr; about $250 at the 1.3 hours one mechanic's guide calls typical for an inline four); midsize 2015 Accord V6 about $153 for the rear bank only (1.1 hr) to about $404 for both banks (2.2 hr); truck 2016 Silverado 5.3L about $213-$322 (1.7-1.9 hr); luxury 2015 BMW 328i about $158-$546 with the gasket set alone (1-3 hr), and about $963 if the whole plastic cover is replaced ($482.85 cover kit plus 3 hours at $160). The lowest totals we can build are $153-$158, in line with the $150 floor, and they pair a list-price gasket with the shortest stated time, so few real quotes will come in that low. The $950 ceiling matches the whole-cover BMW case and sits inside what other sources show for hard engines: one mechanic's guide puts a 2015 Ford Explorer 3.5L at $980-$1,100, and YourMechanic lists a 2015 Volvo S80 at $1,575, so some vehicles will exceed the live top. The range is wide because the job really does vary: the gasket is cheap ($9-$66 here) and almost all of the cost is labor, which runs from about an hour on an easy inline four to five hours or more where an intake manifold or other parts must come off. How solid the labor times are: only one is a manufacturer time for the example vehicle, the Honda warranty flat-rate time of 1.1 hours for the rear bank of the Accord V6, and that procedure also replaces intake manifold gaskets that we did not price. The Accord high end (2.2 hours) is a named mechanic's figure for an Acura with a similar 3.5L V6. The economy and luxury hours are general statements about inline fours (1-3 hours), not times for the Corolla or the BMW; BMW bulletins refer dealers to BMW's own labor system instead of printing a time. The truck hours come from a cost guide's customer-estimate rows for comparable full-size trucks and SUVs, not a manufacturer or book time and not the Silverado. A Hyundai campaign bulletin (2007-2009 Santa Fe 3.3L, front bank gasket plus alternator test and oil protector) allows 1.3 hours, which supports the low end for one bank of a V6. Parts sourcing gaps: the Accord and Silverado each rest on a single priced page, no priced aftermarket set was found for the Silverado, and on the Corolla, Accord and Silverado the genuine gasket at list is cheaper than the aftermarket set, so the low ends are genuine parts. Our mainstream totals sit a little below RepairPal ($375-$514); its labor figure of $288-$423 implies about two to three hours at typical rates, more than the warranty and easy-engine times at our low ends. The web search allowance for this run was used up before the missing items (a second parts source for the Accord and Silverado, a V8 truck time and a BMW time) could be looked for.
extras: A quote often adds spark plug tube seals and cover bolt grommets if the set does not include them, spark plugs or ignition coils that have been soaked in oil, intake manifold gaskets on engines where the manifold comes off to reach the rear cover, engine cleaning to confirm the leak has stopped, shop supplies and sales tax. On V engines the second bank is usually quoted at the same time. A PCV valve built into the cover, or a cracked or warped plastic cover, can turn the job into a whole-cover replacement costing several hundred dollars more. An oil leak diagnosis fee may be charged separately.
